title: Eddeep: a deep-learning framework for fast eddy-current distortion correction in diffusion MRI
abstract: Diffusion MRI (dMRI) relies on diffusion-weighted echo-planar imaging, which is highly susceptible to eddy-current-induced geometric distortions. These distortions vary across diffusion volumes according to gradient strength and direction, causing between-volume misalignment that can bias downstream microstructural analyses. Current state-of-the-art correction methods, such as FSL Eddy, achieve high-quality correction through iterative prediction-correction schemes but are computationally expensive. We propose Eddeep, a deep-learning framework for fast eddy-current distortion correction in dMRI. Eddeep decomposes the problem into two stages. First, a supervised image translation network standardises the appearance of diffusion-weighted and b=0 images, removing contrast differences that hinder reliable registration. Second, an unsupervised registration network estimates both eddy-current distortion and between-volume head motion parameters under a physics-constrained quadratic distortion model, enabling correction in a single forward pass. The method was trained on UK Biobank data and evaluated on both in-domain (UK Biobank) and out-of-domain (Memodyn) datasets. Across a range of complementary metrics, including between-volume jitter, diffusion kurtosis imaging residuals, signal irregularity, and mutual information, Eddeep achieved correction quality comparable to that of FSL Eddy while substantially reducing inference time. These results demonstrate that deep learning can provide accurate and efficient eddy-current distortion correction without relying on iterative optimisation, supporting the development of faster diffusion MRI processing pipelines for large-scale studies and clinical deployment. The code is available at: https://github.com/CIG-UCL/eddeep.

title: Situating Vulnerability: An Ethical Governance Framework for Anthropomorphic AI Interaction
abstract: Large language models increasingly address users in the register of care: they remember personal details, adopt a first-person emotional voice, and sustain relationships across many sessions. This anthropomorphic mode of interaction generates risks that output-level metrics capture poorly, because the same empathic utterance may console one user, entrap a second, and consolidate a delusion in a third. Governance has responded in two ways. Uniform restriction refuses sensitive requests or suppresses empathic phrasing across all outputs; group-targeted protection profiles vulnerable populations and applies stricter or prohibitive rules to them. This article argues that both fail. Uniform restriction mislocates harm in the lexical form of responses rather than in the trajectory of a relationship; group-based protection depends on a list that can never be complete, treats a fluid property as a static attribute of persons, and converts protective attention into stigmatizing labels. Drawing on philosophical work that treats vulnerability as universal, relational, and differentiated, we propose that the unit of ethical governance should be the vulnerability situation rather than the vulnerable group, develop a typology of five situations - physical, emotional, cognitive, autonomy, and relational - and specify seven principles into requirements that guide response calibration without diagnosing or persistently classifying users. The framework relocates AI safety from output control to relational safety.

abstract: We compare the physical properties of inner-Earth asteroid (163693) Atira with the NEOMOD3 population model. Its radar-derived diameter of 4.9 km and absolute magnitude H$_V\simeq$16.4 imply a geometric albedo of p$_V\sim$0.02. Photometry with the Astrophysical Research Consortium 3.5-m telescope and ARCTIC yields g-r=0.49$\pm$0.03, r-i=0.20$\pm$0.02, i-z=0.02$\pm$0.03, a$^\ast$=$-0.05\pm0.03$, and a g-to-i spectral slope of 3.4$\pm$0.9$\%$/100 nm. The photometric reflectance favors a provisional X-type classification; combined with the low albedo, it supports a Tholen P-type interpretation. NEOMOD3 assigns an approximately 66$\%$ probability of delivery through inner Main Belt channels and 26$\%$ to central and outer Main Belt channels. Atira's NEOMOD3 albedo-category probabilities are $0.07\pm0.02$, $0.64\pm0.04$, and $0.29\pm0.04$ for p$_V<$0.1, 0.1$\leq$p$_V<$0.3, and p$_V\geq$0.3, respectively. Across 38 inner-Earth objects, including Atira and 'Ayló'chaxnim, inner Main Belt delivery generally dominates, and intermediate albedo is favored for 33 objects. Atira therefore represents an uncommon low-albedo outcome, compatible with delivery of dark material from the inner Main Belt or more distant primitive populations. Further characterization of inner-Earth asteroids will test whether current population models reproduce their compositional diversity.

title: Instability of exact finite-amplitude acoustic-gravity waves
abstract: Godin (\textit{J. Fluid Mech.}, vol. 767, 2015, pp. 52--64) showed that compressible fluids in a uniform gravity field support finite-amplitude incompressible wave motions, in which every parcel conserves pressure and density, and constructed exact Gerstner-type surface and edge waves, possibly carried by currents. Using the short-wavelength instability method for compressible flows, we show that these waves are linearly unstable above a critical steepness. The stability of each fluid level reduces to a Floquet problem depending on two parameters: the steepness $\mathfrak{e}=e^{ka_2}$ and $ν^2=(1-\mathfrak{e}^2)ν_0^2$, where $ν_0^2=\cos^2α\,N_0^2/Ω^2$, $N_0$ is the buoyancy frequency of the hydrostatic reference state, $α$ the inclination of the plane of motion and $Ω=(gk\cosα)^{1/2}$ the intrinsic orbital frequency. In an isentropic fluid, a level is unstable if $\mathfrak{e}>1/3$, recovering Leblanc's threshold for Gerstner waves (\textit{J. Fluid Mech.}, vol. 506, 2004, pp. 245--254) and extending it to compressible surface and edge waves; weak stable stratification lowers the threshold to $\frac13-\frac{32}{81}ν_0^2+O(ν_0^4)$. In an isothermal atmosphere, $ν_0^2=κ\cosα/(kH)$, where $H$ is the pressure scale height. For horizontal wavelengths near $5.5\,H/\cosα$, principal subharmonic resonance makes the critical steepness vanish. For the fast airglow wave observed by Hecht et al. (\textit{J. Geophys. Res.}, vol. 107, 2002, D20, 4444), which Godin interpreted with his solution, the lidar temperature places the layer in which this interpretation is consistent on this resonance, where the critical steepness is typically 0.1 instead of $1/3$. Instability is confined to a layer beneath the free surface of surface waves and to a wedge at the shoreline of edge waves.

title: Can Event Detectors Leave the Broadcast Camera? Evidence from Tennis
abstract: Ball bounces and racket hits are the events from which tennis statistics are derived, and on monocular video the two are easy to confuse. We release a benchmark of 345 bounce and hit annotations at frame level on eight clips that mix broadcast, fixed elevated, phone and court-level viewpoints, with a frozen development and test split, a confusion-aware matcher, clip-level bootstrap intervals and a blind second annotation of three clips. On it we score supervised precise spotters with published broadcast weights, two zero-shot vision-language models, and RallyArb, an arbitration layer over a ball track and player poses that fits no parameter on event labels. The supervised spotters score near-perfectly on broadcast footage and almost nothing on phone and court-level footage, where the pooled bounce F1 of E2E-Spot is 0.130. RallyArb keeps a bounce F1 above 0.8 on the three phone and court-level clips, two of which were used to tune it, and finds 8 of 11 bounces on the held-out one, but it places hits too far from the contact frame to match human timing. The vision-language models detect events on every viewpoint and miss the contact frame by about 0.1 s. Fine-tuned leave-one-clip-out from its broadcast weights, the spotter reaches about 0.8 bounce F1 on two phone and court-level clips and stays at 0.2 on a grazing phone angle. The annotations, the evaluator and the frozen predictions of every scored row are released.

title: EdgePace: Deadline- and Freshness-Aware LLM Scheduling on Unified-Memory Platforms
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly run on edge devices alongside tasks that continuously process sensor data. In many applications, these foreground tasks prepare observations as inputs to the LLM, whose outputs guide subsequent processing or actions. The observations must be processed by foreground deadlines, and LLM feedback must arrive while its source observations remain useful. Yet the CPU and accelerators share a unified-memory system, so LLM inference can delay foreground processing through memory-bandwidth contention even when compute resources remain available. We present EdgePace, a bandwidth-aware runtime that protects foreground deadlines while sustaining timely LLM feedback. EdgePace creates safe suspension points across prefill and decode, monitors foreground memory demand and stalls at low cost, and schedules inference according to contention risk, deadline slack, and output freshness. We evaluate EdgePace on a OnePlus 13 and three NVIDIA Jetson platforms using multi-camera processing and robotic target tracking. Relative to unmanaged inference, it reduces foreground deadline misses by 24.1%--96.1% while retaining 64.9%--98.5% of LLM throughput. All measured LLM outputs arrive within their task-defined freshness windows. On OnePlus 13, for example, camera deadline misses fall by 91.3% while 90.4% of LLM throughput is retained.

title: A lightweight C Code Generator for Heterogeneous TinyML Systems
abstract: Over the past decade, the significant advancements in artificial intelligence have been closely tied to increasingly sophisticated training frameworks and steadily powerful computing hardware. However, the entire ecosystem remains fragmented. On one hand, models are represented with frameworks dependent formats, while on the other hand, new tailored hardware for accelerating novel operators has continued to emerge. To effectively diminish the transfer costs from training to inference, we propose a lightweight C code generator designed for bare-metal heterogeneous systems that incorporate domain-specific accelerators. Through a comprehensive case study on a RISC-V based radar DSP, we demonstrate that by employing an accelerator with ahead-of-time optimizations like weight tuning and bias fusion, our approach achieves a 2.3 times improvement in inference speed and a 20% reduction in binary size compared to the microTVM flow registered with the same accelerator, thus offering another compelling choice for resource-constrained edge devices. The code is open-sourced in Gitlab.

title: Generative Refinement Learning for Temporal Interpolation in Scientific Machine Learning
abstract: Computationally expensive simulations and real-world observations often provide data at a lower temporal resolution than downstream tasks require. Averaging observations at fixed grid points can introduce errors, and motion estimates alone do not determine how the physical field values change. In this work, we study whether learning to correct a simple numerical interpolation improves the reconstruction of intermediate scientific fields. Our model, interpolative FLow EXpert (iFLEX), first estimates the missing field by taking a weighted average of the two observations at each grid point, giving more weight to the observation closer to the requested time. During training, subtracting this estimate from an observed intermediate field gives the residual that a conditional diffusion model learns to generate. Both observations condition the model, together with the target time, the interval between observations, and available physical parameters. To reconstruct an unobserved intermediate field, the generated residual is added to the weighted average. We evaluate iFLEX on Navier-Stokes Kraichnan turbulence, Shanghai radar precipitation, and sea surface temperature. Across these datasets, iFLEX achieves lower reconstruction error than the evaluated baselines, including optical-flow and diffusion models developed for video frame interpolation in computer vision. In a controlled turbulence comparison at a Reynolds number of 36,000, learning the residual reduces relative Frobenius norm error from about 13.7 for direct field generation to 10.5, with the diffusion backbone and training setup held fixed. Code is available at https://github.com/paulpuren/iflex.

title: The kernel mean embedding of a random probability distribution and its principal components
abstract: Given a random probability distribution \(F\), whose realizations are defined on \(\mathbb R^d\), and a kernel \(k\), our aim is to analyze the properties of the kernel mean embedding, \(μ_F\), of \(F\) as a random element of the corresponding reproducing kernel Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\). This establishes a rigorous framework in which kernel statistical techniques for distributional data can be stated both in the sample and population settings and, thus, the asymptotic properties of sample procedures can be properly established. As an illustration of this approach we focus on the principal components of \(F\). We obtain a general convergence result and the explicit expression of the spectral decomposition for the uncentered covariance operator of a normal probability distribution with a Gaussian distributed expectation. The performance of this kernel principal components procedure is illustrated with simulations and the analysis of the intensity distribution in synthetic aperture radar images.

title: Stochastic Analysis of Laser Phase Noise in Photonics-Assisted Radio Frequency Beamforming
abstract: This paper develops a stochastic model for quantifying the impact of laser phase noise on photonics-assisted radio frequency (RF) beamforming. Unlike conventional deterministic models, the presented theoretical framework captures the statistical randomness associated with the RF array factor of beamforming networks driven by finite-linewidth lasers. Fourier-domain analysis reveals that laser phase noise reshapes the spatial coherence function of such beamforming networks, inducing coherent RF aperture shrinkage, beam-pattern distortion, and directivity degradation. The analysis highlights that beamforming network architectures employing nanosecond-scale optical differential delays can exhibit substantial performance degradation even when driven by commercially available narrow-linewidth (kHz-range) lasers. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that average RF power gain gets downscaled and fluctuations dominate in large-aperture beamforming networks due to phase noise, imposing an upper limit on the maximum achievable RF antenna array-size. The reported results highlight the quantitative performance and scalability limits imposed by laser phase noise in photonics-assisted RF beamforming, offering key design guidelines for implementing large-scale beamforming networks in next-generation wireless communications, sensing, radar, and radio astronomy applications.

title: ICASSP 2026 Radar Acoustic Speech Enhancement (RASE) Challenge
abstract: This paper presents the ICASSP 2026 Radar Acoustic Speech Enhancement (RASE) Grand Challenge, the first community challenge dedicated to benchmarking speech enhancement from millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar vibrometry. The challenge targets realistic through-glass sensing scenarios where microphones are ineffective or impractical. We introduce a curated dataset of paired radar and clean speech recordings, standardized preprocessing, a baseline system, and a secure Codabench-based evaluation framework with unified objective metrics. The RASE Challenge establishes the first public benchmark for radar-based speech enhancement and aims to foster reproducible research in this emerging field.

title: SwAIther-Precip: Lead-Time-Aware Bias Correction Enables Kilometer-Scale Downscaling of Global AI Precipitation Forecasts over Switzerland
abstract: Skillful medium-range precipitation forecasting at kilometer scale remains challenging over complex terrain because precipitation arises from multiscale nonlinear processes that global models cannot explicitly resolve at affordable cost. Global AI weather models can produce skillful medium-range forecasts, but their native 0.25 degrees resolution limits direct use for local hazard applications. Statistical downscaling can help bridge this gap, yet existing approaches often struggle with state-dependent, and especially lead-time-dependent, biases in global forecasts. We introduce SwAIther-Precip, a lead-time-aware downscaling framework that converts coarse-resolution AIFS forecasts into probabilistic km-scale precipitation fields over Switzerland. First, a U-Net conditioned on lead time via feature-wise linear modulation deterministically corrects systematic biases at coarse resolution. This targeted correction enables a cheaper super-resolution stage conditioned only on corrected precipitation, allowing direct training on observations rather than on the full atmospheric state. A diffusion-based model then generates fine-scale spatial variability independently of lead time. Using AIFS forecasts and CombiPrecip radar-gauge observations, SwAIther-Precip reduces CRPS by 48% relative to raw AIFS. The generated fields reproduce observed spatial variability with spectral fidelity above 0.85 at large scales and 0.88 at small scales, corresponding to an effective resolution of approximately 4 km on a 1 km grid for lead times up to 5 days. Training across lead times further improves long-range performance, yielding a 13% CRPS reduction at 6 days relative to lead-time-specific models. These results show that explicitly correcting lead-time-dependent biases before generative super-resolution is key to efficient km-scale probabilistic downscaling of global AI precipitation forecasts.

title: A general extractor for coherent patterns across time-frequency measurements
abstract: Scientific discovery increasingly depends on finding meaningful patterns within volumes of sensor data too large for manual inspection. Existing time-frequency event extractors are often engineered or trained on manually labeled examples for each instrument, which can be laborious and difficult to adapt to new environments. To address this, we introduce TokEye, a reference-free method that learns a general criterion for coherent structure from heterogeneous fusion measurements. A model developed under this method, without retraining, can extract signals from various other fields including marine bioacoustics and wideband radar. It recovers 82.5\% of expert-annotated stellarator signals, detects 78\% of dolphin whistles, and identifies radar events with 81.5\% average precision across six benchmarks, while processing full experimental spectrograms in under one second on a GPU. This transfer across unrelated sensors and physical systems reveals common exploitable structure in time-frequency measurements and establishes a scalable foundation for automated scientific signal discovery.

title: Excursion-set structure factor of the auroral electric field
abstract: A spacecraft crossing the aurora cannot tell whether structures in the field-aligned currents are short-lived or merely small. However, by tracking clusters of coherent radar echoes from aurorae and Fourier-transforming motion-shifted echo pairs across radar snapshots, we can calculate the dynamic structure factor of the point-clouds, thereby quantifying the auroral electric field's spatial power and its persistence from 5 to 40 km, in regions where the radar look-direction is perpendicular to the geomagnetic field. This follows from the fact that coherent E-region radar echoes appear only where the ionospheric electric field exceeds the Farley-Buneman instability threshold, and so a point-target imaging radar naturally samples the field's excursion set; the field's spatiotemporal correlations are discernible from that point process. We find that the echo pattern moves with its cluster: large-scale structures persist for tens of seconds, but scales under 10 km renew within seconds, and conjunctions with Swarm satellite pairs replicate the same scale dependence in field-aligned currents. Coherent radar can thus quantify multi-scale variability in the auroral electric field on Alfvénic timescales.

title: Benchmark Radar: A Living Database and Search Engine for AI Benchmarks and Evaluation
abstract: Benchmark researchers and developers of large language models (LLMs) and other AI systems need to find relevant evaluations, locate their benchmark datasets and code, and understand the settings behind reported scores. We present Benchmark Radar, a living database and search engine for retrieval and discovery of AI benchmarks, covering LLM evaluation, agentic and tool-use benchmarks, coding, reasoning, safety, and domain-specific evaluations. The system combines daily discovery of benchmark papers, repositories, datasets, and releases with a searchable benchmark catalog, mentions in model cards and technical reports, and score histories. It retains source identities and citations so readers can inspect candidate benchmarks and their evaluation evidence. Daily discovery draws on 37 sources: 13 direct connectors and 24 first-party research and engineering feeds. The catalog contains 1,283 source records drawn from 4 benchmark catalogs and 12,916 numeric observations on 790 records. We describe collection and retrieval, audit the full catalog, and examine benchmark saturation, adoption trends, and the limits of score comparisons. A worked example walks through a complete prior-art search, showing how to query the catalog and inspect benchmark evidence when designing a new evaluation. We release the web dashboard with a benchmark leaderboard, a Pareto frontier view of score against measured use, saturation and trend views, daily feeds, downloadable evidence, a command-line interface (CLI) for offline queries, and reproducible analysis.

title: Multi-Functional Chirp Signalling for Next-Generation Multi-Carrier Wireless Networks: Communications, Sensing and ISAC Perspectives
abstract: To meet the increasingly demanding quality-of-service requirements of the next-generation multi-carrier mobile networks, it is essential to design multi-functional signalling schemes facilitating efficient, flexible, and reliable communication and sensing in complex wireless environments. As a compelling candidate, we advocate chirp signalling, beneficially amalgamating sequences (e.g., Zadoff-Chu sequences) with waveforms (e.g., chirp spread spectrum and frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar), given their resilience against doubly selective channels. Besides chirp sequences, a wide range of chirp waveforms is considered, ranging from FMCW to affine frequency-division multiplexing (AFDM), to create a promising chirp multicarrier waveform. This study also highlights the advantages of such waveforms in supporting reliable high-mobility communications, plus integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). Finally, we outline several emerging research directions for chirp signalling designs.

title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: The 2005 polygon conjecture fails for all orders above four
abstract: Let $Λ_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$, equivalently, of stochastic $n\times n$ matrices with off-diagonal entries at most $\frac1n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $Λ_n=S_n$; this holds for $n\le3$. We show that the conjecture fails for every $n\ge5$. The vertices of $S_n$ are eigenvalues of circulant Laplacians built from powers of the directed $n$-cycle. To first order, no perturbation of these circulants moves such an eigenvalue out of $S_n$; however, adding chords with nonconstant weights moves it along an edge of $S_n$ to first order and, with an explicit coefficient, beyond the supporting line of this edge to second order. Consequently, every edge of $S_n$ not incident to $0$ or $1$ contains interior points of $Λ_n$, except possibly, for even $n$, the two horizontal edges, whereas the four edges incident to $0$ or $1$ lie on $\partialΛ_n$. For $n=4$, whose only other edges are horizontal, the question was left open in the previous versions; it has since been settled, $Λ_4=S_4$, by a computer-assisted proof of L. Marshall, after an earlier claim by D.Z. Liu, who also proved that $Λ_n$ is not convex for $n\ge5$. We certify an explicit weighted counterexample for $n=5$, lying only $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ outside $S_5$, and an unweighted one for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with a duplicated vertex. Its eigenvalue outside $S_7$ is also an eigenvalue of the two-chord digraph that ends the above perturbation; for the analogous digraphs of order $n$, the excess is asymptotic to $\frac{π^2}{2n^4}$. We also observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, describe $Λ_n$ in terms of eigenvectors, and prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$.

title: The Limits of Price Discrimination When the Market Is Unknown
abstract: Bergemann, Brooks, and Morris (2015) characterize the consumer and producer surplus pairs that segmentation can produce when the distribution of values is known. I fix only the set of possible values and characterize the pairs that some market and some segmentation can produce. They form a convex polygon. Its outer edge is the largest efficient surplus a market can have when its uniform-price profit is capped, net of that profit, and truncated equal-revenue markets attain it. At the values no segmentation is needed; strictly between two values, reaching the frontier requires splitting a market into two extremal markets. With a continuum of values up to $\bar{v}$, consumer surplus is at most $π\ln(\bar{v}/π)$ when producer surplus (the seller's profit) is $π$, this bound is reached without segmentation, and no market gives consumers more than $\bar{v}/e$.

title: First-order aspects of Artin groups
abstract: We prove several results on the model theory of Artin groups, focusing on Artin groups which are "far from right-angled Artin groups". The first result is that if $C$ is a class of Artin groups whose irreducible components are acylindrically hyperbolic and torsion-free, then the model theory of Artin groups of type $C$ reduces to the model theory of their irreducible components. The second result is that the problem of superstability of a given non-abelian Artin group $A$ reduces to certain dihedral parabolic subgroups of $A$ being $n$-pure in $A$, for certain large enough primes $n \in \mathbb{N}$. The third result is that two spherical Artin groups are elementarily equivalent if and only if they are isomorphic. Finally, we prove that the affine Artin groups of type $\tilde{A}_n$, for $n \geq 4$, can be distinguished from the other simply laced affine Artin groups using existential sentences; this uses known computations of second integral homology together with a direct calculation for simply laced Artin groups under the $K(π,1)$ assumption. These computations provide obstructions to the retractions forced by existential equivalence.

title: Unravelling carbene moiety role in the N-heterocyclic carbene-phosphinidenes coordination chemistry: bonding and reactivity in gold chemistry
abstract: The coordination properties of the emerging class of N-heterocyclic carbene-phosphinidene (NHCP) ligands have been reported to be strongly affected by the carbene (NHC) moiety, but a clear understanding remains strikingly limited. In this work the bonding features and reactivity of 13 NHCP gold hydride complexes, [NHCPAuH], bearing different classes of NHCs have been systematically explored and compared to carbene analogues, using a consistent computational protocol. The analyses reveal that, although the $π$-acceptor ability trend of NHCPs qualitatively parallels that of NHCs, the $σ$-donor ability trend reverses, with more $σ$-donating NHC moieties generating less $σ$-donating NHCP ligands. Concurrently, the nature of the NHC moiety impacts the coordination geometry at the P center, with the CNHC-P-Au bond angle appearing as a structural descriptor to monitor and/or design NHCP ligands with desired $σ$-donor properties. The NHCPs stronger $σ$-donor and weaker $π$-acceptor abilities compared to NHCs and their unique structural flexibility and electronic adaptability have been showcased to be directly controlled by the carbene moiety via modulation of the HOMO lone pair energy and its atomic phosphorous 3p character. The reactivity of [NHCPAuH] complexes with CO2, taken as a probe for potential NHCP applications in small molecule activation processes, demonstrates qualitatively similar mechanisms, with remarkably different activation barriers, which directly correlate with the NHCPs $σ$-donor ability, thus reflecting the high tunability of their bonding properties. This work provides insights and perspectives on the design principle of NHCP ligands, with a spotlight on the pivotal role of NHC moiety in modulating their electronic and steric properties, offering opportunities for burgeoning applications across diverse fields.

title: Caged subsequences in permutations
abstract: Given a sequence $\mathfrak{a}:=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ of reals, a subsequence $\mathfrak{b}=(a_{i_1},\ldots,a_{i_k})$ is said to be "caged" if the largest and smallest among the members of $\mathfrak{b}$ are $a_{i_1}$ and $a_{i_k}$, though not necessarily in that order. In this paper, we consider the problem of maximal caged sequences in permutations $π\in S_n$. We also consider the same problem for a random permutation, both when the permutation is chosen uniformly at random and also when it is picked uniformly at random from among the permutations of rectangular shape, via the RSK correspondence. We also give a $O(n\log n)$ time algorithm to obtain these maximal caged sequences. In addition, we propose a randomized linear time algorithm that gives the length of the maximal caged sequence up to the factor of $(1-o(1))$.

title: First measurement of the masses of the $Υ_1(1D)$ and $Υ_3(1D)$ states and the energy dependence of the cross sections for $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)η$ and $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)π^+π^-$
abstract: We study the processes $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)η$ and $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)π^+π^-$ at center-of-mass energies $\sqrt{s}$=(10.73 -- 11.02) GeV using a $142.5\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ data sample, including 122~fb$^{-1}$ near the $Υ$(10860) peak ($\sqrt{s}$ = 10.866 GeV), collected with the Belle detector at the KEKB asymmetric-energy $e^+e^-$ collider. From the peak sample, the products of Born cross section times branching fraction are obtained for $σ_{\rm Born}(e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)η)$ or $σ_{\rm Born}(e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)π^+π^-)$ and ${\cal B}(Υ_J(1D)\toχ_{b1}γ)$ or ${\cal B}(Υ_J(1D)\toχ_{b2}γ)$ for each $Υ_J(1D)$ state. The corresponding branching fractions for $Υ(10860)$ decays are also obtained. The significances of the $Υ_1(1D)$, $Υ_2(1D)$, and $Υ_3(1D)$ signals are 4.8$σ$, ${>}10σ$, and 3.0$σ$, respectively, including systematic uncertainties. The mass for $Υ_2(1D)$ is measured to be $(10167.0\pm 1.0\pm 0.2)$ MeV/$c^2$, where the first and second uncertainties are statistical and systematic. The mass splittings $Δm_{12}=m(Υ_2(1D))-m(Υ_1(1D))$ and $Δm_{23}=m(Υ_3(1D))-m(Υ_2(1D))$ are $(11.8\pm1.5\pm0.4)$ MeV/$c^2$ and $(7.6\pm2.4\pm0.6)$ MeV/$c^2$, respectively.~We determine the energy dependence of the cross sections for $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)η$ and $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)π^+π^-$ for the $Υ_1(1D)$, $Υ_2(1D)$, and $Υ_3(1D)$ states, combined.

title: On Compositeness of $D_{s0}^*(2317)$ and its decay to $D_sπ^0$
abstract: We demonstrate that the $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)$ can be described as a bound-state pole arising from the coupling between a discrete $c\bar{s}(1^3P_0)$ state and the $DK$ continuum state in the Lee-Friedrichs model. The elementariness and compositeness of the $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)$ are determined to be about $Z:X\approx 51.1 \%:48.9\%$, indicating a nearly equal admixture of compact quark-model state and hadronic molecular components. The decay width of $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)\rightarrow D_s^{+}π^0$ is evaluated within the quark rearrangement framework. The transition $c\bar{s}(1^3P_0)\rightarrow D_sπ^0$ proceeds via the OZI-allowed $c\bar{s}(1^3P_0)-D_sη$ coupling followed by $η-π^0$ mixing, which serves as the primary source of isospin violation in this channel. The coupling between $DK$ and $D_sπ^0$ is computed in a quark rearrangement model, where the isospin violation effect originates from the mass difference between the $D^0K^+$ and $D^+K^0$ thresholds. The parameters of the scheme shares the same ones with those of the underlying potential model and only the vacuum production strength is adjusted to reproduce the physical $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)$ mass. This calculation may shed more insight to the nature of exotic $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)$ state and its isospin-breaking decay properties.

title: On the largest prime factors less than $y$ of consecutive shifted primes
abstract: For an integer $n > 1$, let $P^+(n)$ be the largest prime factor of $n$, and let $P_y^+(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$ not exceeding $y$. One of Erdős and Turán's conjectures asserts that the asymptotic density of integers $n$ satisfying $P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)$ is $1/2$. Furthermore, Wang conjectures that for $x\rightarrow\infty$, one has $\#\{p\leq x:P^+(p-1)<P^+(p+1)\}\sim π(x)/2$. In this paper, we show the following results. For any $3\leq y\ll x^{o(1)}$, for $x\rightarrow\infty$, we have \begin{align*} &\#\{n\leq x:P^+_y(n)<P^+_y(n+1)\}\sim \frac{1}{2}x, \\&\#\{p\leq x:P^+_y(p-1)<P^+_y(p+1)\}\sim \frac{1}{2}π(x), \end{align*} where the first result extends a previous range $3\leq y\ll \exp(\log x/(100\log\log x))$ due to Rivat (2001). For any $0<α<17/32$, let $y=x^α$. Then there exists $h(α)>0$ such that \begin{align*} \#\{p\leq x:P_y^+(p-1)<P_y^+(p+1)\}\geq(h(α)+o(1))π(x). \end{align*} In particular, the function $h$ satisfies $\lim_{α\rightarrow 0^+}h(α)=1/2$. Similar result also holds for $\#\{n\leq x:P_y^+(n)<P_y^+(n+1)\}$, which improves a previous result $\lim_{α\rightarrow 0^+} h(α)=1/4$ due to Wang (2019).

title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ in which $2$ is invertible requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm for multiplication in this algebra costing $O(N \log N)$ arithmetic operations in $R$ and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage when the doubling parameters of $A_n$ are units whose square roots lie in a fixed commutative coefficient algebra $S$ finitely generated as an $R$-module and admitting an $R$-linear map $π\colon S \to R$ with $π(1) = 1$. In particular, over $\mathbb{R}$ and every finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ of odd characteristic, a quadratic field extension contains a square root of every possible doubling parameter, so the algorithm applies to every Cayley-Dickson tower over these fields, and the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ over them is at most $(9n-21)2^n+28$ when $n\ge2$. When the top doubling parameter is a non-square, as in the standard real tower, the bound is $(9n-15)2^{n-1}+10$. To the author's knowledge, the algorithm presented in this paper is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. When $R=\mathbb{R}$ with every doubling parameter equal to $-1$, the real quasilinear schedule uses fewer total arithmetic operations than both direct multiplication and a uniform algorithm of Cariow-Cariowa for $n\ge4$. An implementation for the standard real tower is available in the MIT-licensed C11 library fastCD, with a NumPy-backed Python interface. In single-core benchmarks against direct multiplication and the uniform Cariow-Cariowa method, the quasilinear implementation had the lowest mean time of the three at every tested dimension $N\ge32$, for both single and batched products, and was over $17$ times faster than direct multiplication at $N=1024$.

title: From a symmetry between $e$ and $π$ to the holonomic triangle
abstract: In 2002, the author studied together the recurrences $u_{n+2}=u_{n+1}+u_n/n$ and $v_{n+2}=v_{n+1}/n+v_n$, in which the factor $1/n$ is placed in a symmetric way. The first one leads to $e$ and the second one to $π$, and each of them is classical when taken separately. When $n$ is replaced by $n+m$ in the denominators, with an integer $m\ge0$, the solutions grow like $f(m)\,n$ and $g(m)\sqrt n$, and the connection constants $f(m)$ and $g(m)$, suitably normalized, are explicit linear forms in $1$ and $e$ and in $1$ and $π$. We let $m$ become a complex variable $z$. Then $f$ and $g$ become meromorphic functions of $z$, the connection functions, which satisfy linear functional equations of order two in $z$, as the Gamma function satisfies $Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z)$. They add a third object to the classical pair formed by a P-recursive sequence and its D-finite generating function. We characterize them by their functional equations and their growth, as Wielandt's theorem does for the Gamma function, we show that they are differentially transcendental, and we explain the linear forms at the integers by the solutions excluded by the growth condition. In general, when the coefficients of a linear recurrence in $n$ depend on the parameter only through $n+z$, a translation argument gives a functional equation for the connection constant under the normalization and convergence assumptions of our translation theorem. Conversely, a solution of a linear functional equation with polynomial coefficients which has uniform polynomial growth in a right half-plane is the limit of an explicit P-recursive family of interpolation polynomials, and this applies to all the connection functions given by our existence theorem for coefficients of degree one in $n+z$.

title: Amplituhedra and origami, I: tree level
abstract: We establish a precise correspondence between points of the $m=4$ tree momentum amplituhedron and origami crease patterns. As an application, we prove that the BCFW (Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten) cells triangulate the $m=4$ tree amplituhedron both in momentum space and in momentum-twistor space. As another application, we show that every nondegenerate weighted planar bipartite graph $Γ$ admits a t-embedding, i.e., an embedding of the planar dual of $Γ$ such that the sum of angles of white (equivalently, black) faces around each vertex is equal to $π$.

title: The cohesive and stable Ramsey theorems and proof size over a weak base theory
abstract: We show that over the weak base theory $\mathrm{RCA}_0^*$, cohesive Ramsey's theorem for pairs $\mathrm{CRT}^2_2$ implies exponential closure of the definable cut $\mathrm{I}^0_1$, which is the intersection of all $Σ^0_1$-definable cuts. Consequences include non-elementary proof speedup of $\mathrm{RCA}_0^* + \mathrm{CRT}^2_2$ over $\mathrm{RCA}_0^*$ for $Π_1$ sentences and the unprovability of $\mathrm{CRT}^2_2$ in $\mathrm{RCA}_0^* + \mathrm{CAC}$. On the other hand, we show that $\mathrm{RCA}_0^* + \mathrm{SRT}^2_2$, where $\mathrm{SRT}^2_2$ is stable Ramsey's theorem for pairs, is polynomially simulated by $\mathrm{RCA}_0^*$ with respect to proofs of $\forall Π^0_3$ sentences. Nevertheless, $\mathrm{SRT}^2_2$ also implies a nontrivial property of $\mathrm{I}^0_1$, specifically closure under functions of quasipolynomial growth rate.

title: Coanalytic subfields and bases of prescribed dimension
abstract: Assume $V=L$. We prove two uniform theorems producing coanalytic sets of prescribed Hausdorff dimension in Euclidean space. The first concerns countable families of partial operations of finite arity on $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose evaluation is hyperarithmetic and which are tame in each vector variable separately. For such families a single lightface $Π^1_1$ relation yields strictly increasing, left-continuous chains of proper sets closed under the operations, one of each Hausdorff dimension in $[0,n]$, uniformly in the family and in $n$; no exchange property of the closure is needed. As an application, there are coanalytic proper subfields of $\mathbb{R}$ of every Hausdorff dimension in $[0,1]$. The second theorem constructs coanalytic bases of every possible Hausdorff dimension for effectively coded pregeometries. As an application, there are coanalytic Hamel bases of $\mathbb{R}^n$ and transcendence bases of $\mathbb{C}$ of every Hausdorff dimension in $[0,n]$ and $[0,2]$, respectively.

title: Identifying $Σ(1380)$ and $Σ(1430)$ in the $J/ψ\to Λπ\barΣ$ reaction
abstract: We study the $J/ψ\to Λπ\barΣ$ reaction by looking at the $π^+ Λ$ mass distribution at low energies, in search of signals for the low lying $Σ^+$ excited states. Apart from a clear signal of the $Σ(1385) (3/2^+)$ state, we find a smaller peak for the predicted $Σ(1430) (1/2^-)$, which has already been confirmed by the Belle Collaboration. A first analysis, considering only the $πΛ$ interaction, shows that the low energy part of the spectrum is better reproduced including contributions from the $Σ(1430)$ and the predicted $Σ(1380)(1/2^-)$ state that has been claimed before from analyses of different experiments. However, when we consider the $π\barΣ$ interaction the need for the $Σ(1380)$ disappears.

title: Optimal In-context Adaptivity and Distributional Robustness of Transformers
abstract: We study in-context learning problems where a Transformer is pretrained on tasks drawn from a mixture distribution $π=\sum_{α\in\mathcal{A}} λ_α π_α$, called the pretraining prior, in which each mixture component $π_α$ is a distribution on tasks of a specific difficulty level indexed by $α$. Our goal is to understand the performance of the pretrained Transformer when evaluated on a different test distribution $μ$, consisting of tasks of fixed difficulty $β\in\mathcal{A}$, and with potential distribution shift relative to $π_β$, subject to the chi-squared divergence $χ^2(μ,π_β)$ being at most $κ$. In particular, we consider nonparametric regression problems with random smoothness, and multi-index models with both random smoothness and random effective dimension. We prove that a large Transformer pretrained on sufficient data achieves the optimal rate of convergence corresponding to the difficulty level $β$, uniformly over test distributions $μ$ in the chi-squared divergence ball. Thus, the pretrained Transformer is able to achieve faster rates of convergence on easier tasks and is robust to distribution shift at test time. Finally, we prove that even if an estimator had access to the test distribution $μ$, the convergence rate of its expected risk over $μ$ could not be faster than that of our pretrained Transformers, thereby providing a more appropriate optimality guarantee than minimax lower bounds.

title: Rank-Two Drinfeld Modules over Elliptic Coordinate Rings
abstract: Let ${\mathbf A}$ be the affine coordinate ring of $E\setminus\{\infty\}$, where $E$ is an elliptic curve over $\mathbb F_q$ and $\infty$ is rational. We solve the rank-two case of the open problem of explicitly classifying sign-normalized Drinfeld ${\mathbf A}$-modules in generic characteristic with a fixed determinant motive; the classification for rank greater than two remains open. Outside an explicit exceptional locus, the rank-two Drinfeld modules are parametrized by the open modular curve $Y^{q+1}=π(X)$ with $Y\neq0$. The polynomial $π$ is squarefree, and the smooth projective completion of this curve has genus $q^2$. The roots of $π$ split into two types. Above roots of the first type, all coefficient functions extend regularly, and their extensions yield exactly the exceptional modules. Roots of the second type correspond to cusps of the modular curve; above these roots, the coefficient family has poles.

title: Semiclassical Band Splitting in the Infinite Chern Band Model
abstract: We study the two lowest Bloch bands of the infinite Chern band model of Tan and Devakul in the semiclassical limit. When the Berry curvature parameter is an odd multiple of $π$, we show that the first two bands are exponentially close and meet at exactly one Dirac point. The proof combines Agmon estimates and WKB approximations for a matrix Schrödinger operator whose lowest potential eigenvalue has two wells. Geometric properties of the Agmon distance allow us to compute the leading tunneling coefficients by the method of stationary phase. We provide numerical computations to illustrate the asymptotic formula and support the conjecture that the two bands remain separated for other values of the Berry curvature parameter.

title: Schubert puzzles and integrability III: separated descents
abstract: In paper I of this series we gave positive formulae for expanding the product $\mathfrak S^π\mathfrak S^ρ$ of two Schubert polynomials, in the case that both $π,ρ$ had shared descent set of size $\leq 3$. Here we introduce and give positive formulae for two new classes of Schubert product problems: separated descent in which $π$'s last descent occurs at (or before) $ρ$'s first, and almost separated descent in which $π$'s last two descents occur at (or before) $ρ$'s first two respectively. In both cases our puzzle formulae extend to $K$-theory (multiplying Grothendieck polynomials), and in the separated descent case, to equivariant $K$-theory. The two formulae arise (via quantum integrability) from fusion of minuscule quantized loop algebra representations in types $A$, $D$ respectively.

title: Dimension-Independent Convergence of Underdamped Langevin Monte Carlo in KL Divergence
abstract: Underdamped Langevin dynamics (ULD) is a widely-used sampler for Gibbs distributions $π\propto e^{-V}$, and is often empirically effective in high dimensions. However, existing non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for discretized ULD typically scale polynomially with the ambient dimension $d$, leading to vacuous bounds when $d$ is large. The main known dimension-free result concerns the randomized midpoint discretization in Wasserstein-2 distance (Liu et al.,2023), while dimension-independent guarantees for ULD discretizations in KL divergence have remained open. We close this gap by proving the first dimension-free KL divergence bounds for discretized ULD. Our analysis refines the KL local error framework (Altschuler et al., 2025) to a dimension-free setting and yields bounds that depend on $\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{H})$, where $\mathbf{H}$ upper bounds the Hessian of $V$, rather than on $d$. As a consequence, we obtain improved iteration complexity for underdamped Langevin Monte Carlo relative to overdamped Langevin methods in regimes where $\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{H})\ll d$.

title: Topological zero-reflection points in multi-terminal quantum wire junctions
abstract: We study scattering in noninteracting multi-terminal quantum wire junctions and show that junctions with dihedral symmetry can exhibit exact zero-reflection points for $N \ge 4$ terminals. By analyzing the scattering matrix, we identify these reflectionless points in the $(E,t')$ parameter space, where $E$ is the incident particle energy and $t'$ is the junction hopping amplitude. These points exhibit an even-odd dependence on $N$ and converge asymptotically to a common limiting value in the large-$N$ limit. We show that the reflectionless points are characterized by an integer winding number associated with the phase of the reflection amplitude, providing a topological description for their stability against weak on-site disorder. title: Dynamical Coulomb effects on charged-pion HBT-radius splitting in central Au+Au collisions at few-GeV energies
abstract: The pair transverse momentum ($k_T$) and collision-energy ($\sqrt{s_{NN}}$) dependent difference between $π^{+}π^{+}$ and $π^{-}π^{-}$ femtoscopic correlations was observed by the HADES and STAR Collaborations. Using the UrQMD model and the CRAB programme, three transport scenarios that successively include baryon-baryon, baryon-meson, and meson-meson Coulomb interactions are considered. The calculations reproduce the main $k_{T}$ and $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ dependences of the radii. Baryon--meson Coulomb interactions generate most of the additional charge splitting in the microscopic calculation. The residual-source treatment also enhances the longitudinal and sideward radius ratios relative to the reference, whereas the outward ratio changes little, and the enhancement generally decreases with increasing $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$. Within the present framework, this contribution does not fully account for the data, motivating further investigation of the charged-source geometry and its interplay with strong-interaction dynamics.

title: On the Vertices of Delta-modular Polyhedra
abstract: Let $P$ be a polytope defined by the system $A x \leq b$, where $A \in R^{m \times n}$, $b \in R^m$, and $\text{rank}(A) = n$. We give a short geometric proof of the following tight upper bound on the number of vertices of $P$: $$ n! \cdot \fracΔ{Δ_{\text{average}}} \cdot \text{vol}(B_2) \sim \frac{1}{\sqrt{πn}} \cdot \left(\frac{2 π}{e}\right)^{n/2} \cdot n^{n/2} \cdot \fracΔ{Δ_{\text{average}}}, $$ where $Δ$ is the maximum absolute value of $n \times n$ subdeterminants of $A$, and $Δ_{\text{average}}$ is the average absolute value of subdeterminants of $A$ corresponding to a triangulation of $P$'s normal fan. Assuming that $A$ is integer, such polyhedra are called $Δ$-modular polyhedra. Note that in the integer case, the bound can be simplified via the inequality $Δ_{\text{average}} \geq Δ_{\min} \geq 1$, where $Δ_{\min}$ is the minimum absolute value of subdeterminants of $A$ corresponding to feasible bases of $A x \leq b$. For this, we prove and use a symmetric variant of Macbeath's theorem. Additionally, we give a direct argument based on prior results in the field, showing that the graph diameter of $P$ is bounded by $O\bigl(n^3 \cdot \fracΔ{Δ_{\min}} \cdot \ln (n \fracΔ{Δ_{\min}}) \bigr)$. Thus, both characteristic of $P$ are linear in $Δ/Δ_{\min}$. From an algorithmic perspective, we demonstrate that: Given $A \in Q^{m \times n}$, $b \in Q^m$, and an initial feasible solution to $A x \leq b$, the convex hull of $P$ can be constructed in $O(n)^{n/2} \cdot m^2 \cdot \fracΔ{Δ_{\text{average}}}$ operations. For simple polyhedra, the dependence on $m$ reduces to linear; Given $A \in Z^{m \times n}$ and $b \in Q^m$, the number $|P \cap Z^n|$ can be computed in $O(n)^n \cdot \frac{Δ^4}{Δ_{\text{average}}}$ arithmetic operations.

title: Study of $φ\to K\bar{K}$ in the amplitude analysis of $D^{+}\to K_{S}^{0}K_{L}^{0}π^{+}$

title: Quantum theory of photonic vortices and quantum statistics of twisted photons
abstract: The topological charge of a photonic vortex is an essential quantity in singular optics and the critical parameter to characterize the vorticity of twisted light. However, the definition of the photonic topological charge remains elusive. Here we put forth a theoretical formalism to provide a comprehensive treatment of photonic vortices. We introduce quantum operators for the photon current density and helicity current density based on the continuity equations from the paraxial Helmholtz equation. Our formalism allows us to introduce flow velocity and circulation for photonic currents in parallel to their counterparts in superfluids. The quantized circulation of the photonic currents is conserved during propagation and it gives an explicit definition of the photonic topological charge as the winding number of a photonic vortex. In particular, we predict helicity current generated pure helicity vortices, in which the photon current vanishes. Finally, we show an interesting effect that the quantum statistics of twisted photon pairs are essentially determined by their spin states.

title: Universal Quantum Gate Set for Multi-Mode Schrödinger Cat States Stabilized by Non-Local Dissipation Engineering
abstract: Schrödinger cat states provide a hardware-efficient platform for bosonic quantum error correction by encoding logical information in protected manifolds of harmonic oscillators. While previous work has demonstrated the dissipative stabilization of multi-mode Schrödinger cat states as robust quantum memories, a framework for universal quantum computation has remained unavailable. Here we work towards this by introducing a universal gate set for dissipatively stabilized multi-mode cat qubits as a necessary resource for computation. Using a chain of Kerr non-linear oscillators coupled through engineered non-local dissipation and an effective low-dimensional description, we show how single-qubit control can be achieved through arbitrary rotation around the $X$-axis and $π/2$-rotation around the $Z$-axis. We further show how coupling two such stabilized arrays through just one oscillator on each respective array enables coherent entangling operations through implementation of the $XX_{π/2}$ gate. Numerical simulations demonstrate high-fidelity gate dynamics and entanglement generation under realistic parameters. Finally, we analyze the effects of induced and intrinsic photon loss, disorder, and the validity regime of the effective low-dimensional theory. Our results establish dissipatively stabilized multi-mode Schrödinger cat states as a potential architecture for universal bosonic quantum computation.

title: Thermal Hall Signatures of Distinct Schwinger-Boson Flux Sectors on the Honeycomb Lattice
abstract: Thermal transport offers a bulk probe of charge-neutral excitations in frustrated magnets. It remains challenging, however, to determine whether such transport can distinguish different parton mean-field structures of the same spin system. This question is particularly relevant on the honeycomb lattice, where distinct $0$-flux, $π$-flux, and chiral $π/2$-flux sectors have been proposed. In this paper, we compare self-consistent saddle-point solutions in these three sectors for a frustrated $J_1-J_2$ Heisenberg model with a next-nearest-neighbor Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and a perpendicular magnetic field. Using finite-temperature Schwinger-boson mean-field theory and the Kubo formula for bosonic Bogoliubov-de Gennes systems, we evaluate the intrinsic spinon thermal Hall conductivity. At a common parameter point where all three branches remain gapped, the $0$-flux response is positive and the $π$-flux response is negative for $D>0$ and $h>0$ under the sign conventions used in this paper, whereas the $π/2$-flux response changes sign with increasing temperature. We further show that a projective symmetry combining a sixfold rotation with time reversal forces the zero-field response of a fixed chiral $π/2$-flux domain to vanish. Within the mean-field regime examined in this paper, the sign and temperature dependence of $κ_{xy}/T$ therefore provide a flux-sensitive transport signature.

title: On the Optimal Sample Complexity of Offline Multi-Armed Bandits with KL Regularization
abstract: Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization is widely used in offline decision-making and offers several benefits, motivating recent work on the sample complexity of offline learning with respect to KL-regularized performance metrics. Nevertheless, the exact sample complexity of KL-regularized offline learning remains largely from fully characterized. In this paper, we study this question in the setting of multi-armed bandits (MABs). We provide a sharp analysis of KL-PCB (Zhao et al., 2026), showing that it achieves a sample complexity of $\tilde{O}(ηSAC^{π^*}/ε)$ under large regularization $η= \tilde{O}(ε^{-1})$, and a sample complexity of $\tildeΩ(SAC^{π^*}/ε^2)$ under small regularization $η= \tildeΩ(ε^{-1})$, where $η$ is the regularization parameter, $S$ is the number of contexts, $A$ is the number of arms, $C^{π^*}$ policy coverage coefficient at the optimal policy $π^*$, $ε$ is the desired sub-optimality, and $\tilde{O}$ and $\tildeΩ$ hide all poly-logarithmic factors. We further provide a pair of sharper sample complexity lower bounds, which matches the upper bounds over the entire range of regularization strengths. Overall, our results provide a nearly complete characterization of offline multi-armed bandits with KL regularization.

title: THz-Driven Floquet Spin Valve-Modulator
abstract: Within the scattering matrix ($S$-matrix) framework adapted to the high-frequency Floquet--Magnus formalism based on the length gauge, we investigate spin-dependent quantum transport in a 1D quantum ring with an asymmetric ($π/2$) configuration of quantum point contacts. We demonstrate the realization of a contactless electromagnetic analog of the Datta--Das spin field-effect transistor with ferromagnetic leads operating at zero static magnetic field. It is shown that an off-resonance terahertz (THz) field enables high-precision switching between spin channels without altering the static parameters of the nanostructure. Driven by an electronic Vernier effect, the quantum interference in the asymmetric geometry yields a selective spin phase rotator alongside an ultra-high-contrast current-suppression regime (``optical shutter''). The proposed architecture is fundamentally robust against multiphoton leakage sidebands, offering a thermally immune, high-speed alternative to conventional semiconductor static spin transistors.

title: Interlayer Phase Locking and Sliding Select Topological Melting Channels in Superconducting Bilayers
abstract: Topological transitions in coupled superconducting layers are intertwined: an elementary vortex in one layer carries both common and relative phase winding. We study a Josephson-coupled bilayer in an in-plane magnetic field using renormalization-group analysis and Monte Carlo simulations of the compact layer phases. The field drives Pokrovsky--Talapov (PT) entry of interlayer solitons, and free-energy calculations in fixed soliton sectors show PT square-root scaling over the sampled densities at finite temperature. Interlayer phase locking and sliding then select distinct Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT)-like melting channels. The locked commensurate phase melts through same-vorticity layer pairs when the geometric-mean common helicity modulus $Υ_{+,g}$ reaches $T/(2π)$, with layer correlation exponent $η_l=1/4$. A stable sliding incommensurate phase melts through elementary layer vortices on a line of BKT fixed points, where $Υ_{+,g}+Υ_{-,g}=2T/π$ and $η_l$ is set by the ratio of the relative and common moduli. When the relative helicity modulus is identified with the relative-phase stiffness, our simulations agree with this prediction, and the common superfluid stiffness at incommensurate melting is nearly twice its value at commensurate melting. Near soliton entry, however, the dilute sliding state is unstable to opposite-vorticity layer pairs. Our results connect PT soliton entry with field-tunable BKT-like melting and identify the pair-stability condition that links them.

title: -Properties, Uniformly Convexity and Uniform Ball Coverings Properties
abstract: In this paper, we prove a sufficient condition for the uniform ball-covering property of closed operator subspaces invariant under selected truncations. We use uniform convexity of the range space and near-contractive finite-rank projection approximations to obtain quantitative coverings with finite-rank centres whenever the truncated images are separable. A weak-star version gives the same covering parameters for quotients by arbitrary weak-star closed subspaces. In the completely bounded setting, the covering parameters are independent of the matrix level. Applications include operator-valued Schur multipliers and, for $1<p<\infty$, prescribed-support Fourier multipliers on countable amenable groups and finitely generated free groups. The Fourier coverings have finite-support centres in the given operator or completely bounded norms. An endpoint example shows failure of the ball-covering property at $p=1,\infty$.

title: Transformer-based machine learning using low-level calorimeter signals for collimated photon identification at collider experiments
abstract: Electromagnetic calorimeters provide essential information for reconstructing and selecting both Standard Model (SM) and potential beyond the SM physics events at high-energy particle colliders. The fine-grained segmentation of modern calorimeters captures rich information about the internal structure of particle showers, much of which is discarded by conventional high-level reconstruction methods. In this work, we leverage calorimeter cell-level information to classify highly collimated diphoton signatures, arising from the decay of light axion-like particles, from isolated single-photon showers. We systematically compare a range of machine learning architectures, spanning high-level, shower shape variable-based approaches and direct cell-level methods. Cell-level machine learning shows significantly superior classification ability, with a Transformer in particular representing the best performance among six different architectures studied, and an MLP Mixer representing a resource-constrained alternative for potential real-time, trigger-level applications. Beyond classification, the Transformer model developed enables direct invariant mass regression from calorimeter cells, improving the characterization of light resonances and providing an additional handle in reducing the $π^0$ and $η$ fake photon backgrounds. These results demonstrate that cell-level machine learning methods can extend calorimeter-based particle identification and performance well beyond the capabilities of current conventional techniques.

title: Quantum field theory for spin operator of the photon
abstract: All elementary particles in nature can be classified as fermions with half-integer spin and bosons with integer spin. Within quantum electrodynamics (QED), even though the spin of the Dirac particle is well defined, there exist open questions on the quantized description of spin of the gauge field particle -- the photon. Using quantum field theory, we discover the quantum operators for the spin angular momentum (SAM) $\boldsymbol{S}_{M}=(1/c)\int d^{3}x\boldsymbolπ\times\boldsymbol{A}$ and orbital angular momentum (OAM) $\boldsymbol{L}_{M}=-(1/c)\int d^{3}xπ^μ\boldsymbol{x}\times\boldsymbol{\nabla}A_μ$ of the photon, where $π^μ$ is the conjugate canonical momentum of the gauge field $A^μ$. We also reveal a perfect symmetry between the angular momentum commutation relations for Dirac fields and Maxwell fields. We derive the well-known OAM and SAM of classical electromagnetic fields from the above defined quantum operators. Our work shows that the spin and OAM operators commute which is important for simultaneously observing and separating the SAM and OAM. The correct commutation relations of orbital and spin angular momentum of the photon have applications in quantum optics, topological photonics as well as nanophotonics and can be extended in the future for the spin structure of nucleons.

title: Eigenvalue-by-Eigenvalue Comparison of a Sierra--Rodríguez-Laguna-Type Spectrum with the Riemann Zeros

title: Sharp noncommutative Hilbert and Riesz inequalities: classification and spectral corrections
abstract: For every $1<p<\infty$, with $p^*=\max\{p,p/(p-1)\}$, we determine the sharp Hilbert norm $C_p=\cot(π/(2p^*))$ on $L^p(\mathbb{R};\mathcal{S}_p)$ and the sharp uniform bound $D_p=\csc(π/p)$ for retained and strict Riesz projections of maximal subdiagonal algebras in finite tracial von Neumann algebras. The Hilbert value is also the common Fourier--Schur completely bounded norm. For finite matrices, a nonnegative logarithmic determinant defect connects Heinävaara's tracial joint spectral measure to eigenvalues. The resulting transfer identity classifies finite signed real ridge inequalities on nilpotents and identifies their least additive eigenvalue corrections. A dual theorem characterizes weak-* limits of weighted angular measures of finite nilpotents. title: Global coalitions in graphs
abstract: Let $G=(V, E)$ be a graph. A subset $S \subseteq V$ is called a global dominating set of $G$ if it is a dominating set of both $G$ and its complement $\overline{G}$. Two disjoint subsets $V_1, V_2 \subseteq V$ form a global coalition if neither $V_1$ nor $V_2$ is a global dominating set, but their union $V_1 \cup V_2$ is. A global coalition partition (abbreviated $gc$-partition) of $G$ is a vertex partition $π$ of $V(G)$ such that every class of $π$ forms a global coalition with some other class of $π$. The global coalition number $GC(G)$ is the maximum cardinality of a $gc$-partition of $G$. In this paper, we initiate the study of these concepts. We prove that every graph of order at least two admits a $gc$-partition, give general lower bounds on $GC(G)$, and bound the number of global coalitions in which a single class of a $gc$-partition can be involved. We show that $GC(G)$ coincides with the coalition number $C(G)$ whenever $G$ is disconnected or has radius at least three, and consequently that $GC(G)=C(\overline{G})$ for every join of two graphs. We determine the global coalition number of complete multipartite graphs with at most three parts, wheels, fans, paths, cycles and trees of radius two, characterise the graphs $G$ with $GC(G)=|V(G)|$ in terms of antitwins, relate global coalitions to perfect coalitions, and study unicyclic graphs of radius at most two. Finally, we interpret $gc$-partitions in the language of fair division of indivisible goods and pose several open problems.\\ \textbf{2020 Mathematics Subject Classification:} 05C69, 91B32.\\ \textbf{JEL Classification:} C72, C78, D63.\\ \textbf{Keywords}: Global domination, coalition, global coalition partition, antitwins, trees, unicyclic graphs, fair division.

title: Stringent limits on $C\!PT$- and Lorentz-invariance violation from $B_s^0$ meson decays
abstract: Tests of fundamental symmetries, such as $C\!PT$ and Lorentz invariance, provide sensitive probes of physics beyond the standard quantum-field-theory framework. Possible violations of these symmetries are investigated through interference effects in decays of $B_s^0$ mesons to $D_s^-π^{+}$ states. The analysis uses proton-proton collision data collected with the LHCb detector in 2015-2018 at a centre-of-mass energy of $13~\mathrm{TeV}$, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $6~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$. The results are interpreted within the Standard Model Extension framework, yielding sensitivities to the Lorentz-violating parameter $Δa_μ$ at the ${\cal O}(10^{-14})\,\mathrm{GeV}$ level. Without assuming Lorentz-invariance violation, the $C\!PT$-violating parameter $z$ in the $B_s^0$ system is measured to be $\mathcal{R}e(z) = 0.018 \pm 0.016 \pm 0.003$ and $\mathcal{I}m(z) = 0.003 \pm 0.004 \pm 0.002$, where the first uncertainties are statistical and the second systematic. These results represent the most precise constraints on $C\!PT$ violation in the $B_s^0$ system.

title: Nonsymmorphic Time-Reversal-Doubled Axion Insulators
abstract: The axion insulator exhibits a topological magnetoelectric effect characterized by an axion angle $θ=π$, while the time-reversal-doubled axion insulator (T-DAXI) can be viewed as two copies of an axion insulator related by time-reversal symmetry. In this work, we show that a nonsymmorphic topological crystalline insulator with glide (or screw) symmetry can host the nonsymmorphic T-DAXI phase, diagnosed by the nontrivial hourglass (screw) invariant $δ_h=1$ ($δ_s=1$). In this phase, the partial axion angles ($θ^\pm=π$) are quantized by the glide and/or screw symmetry, and the gapped surfaces realize half-quantized quantum spin Hall states. Furthermore, we show that nonsymmorphic T-DAXIs also exhibit the spin-magnetoelectric effect. Namely, an external magnetic field can induce a topological nonlocal spin polarization in real space. When the magnetic field is time-periodic, this leads to an alternating spin current detectable in experiment. Using ab initio calculations, we demonstrate that mixed bismuth monohalides Bi4Br3I and Bi4BrI3 realize the nonsymmorphic T-DAXIs. Our findings not only reveal the symmetry-enforced T-DAXIs in nonsymmorphic topological crystalline insulators, but also demonstrate the spin-magnetoelectric effect as a detectable topological spin response in nonsymmorphic T-DAXIs.

title: Factorization in deep inelastic scattering at Björken limit: Reduction to (1+1)D integrable models
abstract: We study the small-$x$ behavior of the proton structure function $F_2(x,Q^2)$ using the combined HERA inclusive deep-inelastic-scattering data and compare it with exact structure functions obtained in integrable quantum field theories. The data are described by a local power law, $F_2(x,Q^2)=A(Q^2)x^{-γ(Q^2)}$, where the exponent $γ(Q^2)$ increases smoothly with the hard scale. We show that this running exponent is well described by a simple renormalization-group crossover form and is compatible with the illustrative limiting value $C=γ(\infty)\simeq0.431$. This reference belongs to the sine-Gordon power-law universality class among the exactly solvable possibilities and corresponds to the coupling $β^2/π=16/(3-C)\simeq6.23$. The sine-Gordon-constrained fit gives a quantitatively accurate description of the HERA $F_2$ surface, with reduced $χ^2$ close to unity, and is cross-checked with the overlapping final HERA reduced-cross-section data. These results indicate that the small-$x$ growth observed in deep inelastic scattering is naturally organized by a sine-Gordon-type universality class, while the finite-$Q^2$ dependence is controlled by a smooth crossover toward the corresponding asymptotic exponent.

title: Q-MMR: Off-Policy Evaluation via Recursive Reweighting and Moment Matching
abstract: We present a novel theoretical framework, Q-MMR, for off-policy evaluation in finite-horizon MDPs. Q-MMR learns a set of scalar weights, one for each data point, such that the reweighted rewards approximate the expected return under the target policy. The weights are learned inductively in a top-down manner via a moment matching objective against a value-function discriminator class. Notably, and perhaps surprisingly, a data-dependent finite-sample guarantee for general function approximation can be established under only the realizability of $Q^π$, with a dimension-free bound -- that is, the error does not depend on the statistical complexity of the function class. We also establish connections to several existing methods, such as importance sampling and linear FQE. Further theoretical analyses shed new light on the nature of coverage, a concept of fundamental importance to offline RL.

title: Probing New Physics with $b \to u \ell ν_{\ell}$ induced decays
abstract: We analyze $B^- \to μ^- \barν_μ$, $\bar{B}^0 \to π^+ μ^-\barν_μ$, and $B^- \to ρ^0 μ^- \barν_μ$ decays using the data on binned branching fractions recently measured by Belle II Collaboration for the semileptonic modes. title: Chromatic Ramsey numbers and two-color Turán densities
abstract: Given a graph $G$, its $2$-color Turán number $\mathrm{ex}^{(2)}(n,G)$ is the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph, such that the edges can be colored with two colors avoiding a monochromatic copy of $G$. Let $π^{(2)}(G)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathrm{ex}^{(2)}(n,G)/\binom{n}{2}$ be the $2$-color Turán density of $G$. What real numbers in the interval $(0,1)$ are realized as the $2$-color Turán density of some graph? It is known that $π^{(2)}(G)=1-(R_χ(G)-1)^{-1}$, where $R_χ(G)$ is the chromatic Ramsey number of $G$. Burr, Erdős, and Lovász showed that $(k-1)^2+1\leq{R_χ(G)}\leq{R(k)}$, for any $k$-chromatic graph $G$, where $R(k)$ is the classical Ramsey number. However, it is an open problem to determine how many distinct values between $(k-1)^{2}+1$ and $R(k)$ can be realized as $R_χ(G)$ of some $k$-chromatic graph $G$ for general $k$. In this paper, among others, we prove that there are $Ω(k)$ different values of $R_χ(G)$ among $k$-chromatic graphs $G$. This sheds more light onto the possible $2$-color Turán densities of graphs.

title: Topological multicomponent superconductivity with sizable $s$-wave admixture in twisted bilayer cuprates
abstract: We investigate multicomponent superconductivity in twisted bilayer cuprates with order parameter $s+d_1 e^{iφ_1}+d_2 e^{iφ_2}$, where $s=s_1+s_2$ is the layer-symmetric $s$-wave pairing and $d_i$ is the $d$-wave pairing in layer $i$. When $φ_1-φ_2\neq 0,π$, this three-component state spontaneously breaks time-reversal and $C_4$ rotational symmetries and can realize a topologically nontrivial phase. We further identify nematic Kerr anisotropy as a key signature distinguishing it from $s+id$ and $d_1+e^{iφ}d_2$, and find that its Josephson critical current remains sizable near the $45^{\circ}$ twist. Our results show that $s$-wave pairing does not preclude chiral topological superconductivity, pointing to twisted cuprates as a more robust platform than previously appreciated.

title: Form factors and weak decays of $Λ_b\toΛ_c^*(2595)$ and $Ξ_b\toΞ_c^*(2790)$
abstract: In this article, we reanalyze the mass and pole residue of $Λ$-type singly heavy baryons with spin-parity $J^P=1/2^{\pm}$ using two-point QCD sum rules. Our estimates for the branching ratios of $Λ_b\toΛ^*_c(2595)\ell\barν_\ell$ are comparable with the experimental data and other theoretical results. These results can provide valuable references for future measurements. In addition, we present predictions for several observables in these semileptonic decays, including the lepton universality ratio, the forward-backward asymmetry $A_{FB}$, and the asymmetry parameter $α$, which can provide useful references for future experiments to test the Standard Model and probe new physics beyond it.

title: Iterative Policy Optimization: Batch-Online Multi-Turn RL via Single-Turn RL
abstract: Practical LLM agents often operate over multi-turn conversations where success is determined only after the full interaction ends. Most multi-turn RL methods train via on-policy rollouts, but unlike in single-turn RL, the policy cannot produce a trajectory alone, since an external environment must respond after each agent turn. For conversational agents, this environment is a user, but real users are generally unavailable inside the training loop and simulated users are difficult to build faithfully. Separately, real-world deployment is rarely fully online or fully offline. The common production pattern is called batch online, where the current policy is deployed to collect a batch of interaction data, then retrained on that batch and redeployed. We show that this batch-online setting creates an opportunity for applying the classical approximate policy iteration algorithm. Our central observation is that running standard token-level, single-turn GRPO with a learned turn-level $Q$-function as the reward model is a policy improvement step for the multi-turn problem. Building on this, we present Iterative Policy Optimization (IterPO), which alternates between fitting $Q^π$ from logged Monte Carlo returns via standard reward modeling (policy evaluation) and running single-turn GRPO against $Q^π$ (policy improvement). During policy improvement, the learned $Q^π$ scores candidate responses by their expected downstream return, avoiding the need for simulator rollouts of the remaining conversation. Overall, this allows us to do principled multi-turn RL using only single-turn RL methods without an interactive environment or user simulator inside the training loop. We demonstrate the effectiveness of IterPO on six multi-turn negotiation environments.

title: Counterexamples to a dimension-free variant of Erdős's diameter conjecture for separated distances
abstract: Erdős asked about the least possible diameter of an $n$-point set in Euclidean space when any two pairwise distances differ by at least $1$. We consider the uniform-in-dimension variant of his question, in which the dimension $d$ may grow with $n$ and the error term is independent of $d$, and answer it in the negative by an explicit construction. For every prime power $q$, we construct a set $\mathcal X_n$ of $n=q+1$ points in $\mathbb R^{q^2+q}=\mathbb R^{n^2-n}$ such that the $\binom{n}{2}$ pairwise distances are mutually at least $1$ apart, yet $$\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal X_n)\le \Bigl(1-\frac{1}{π^2}+o(1)\Bigr)n^2.$$ The construction combines a Singer cyclic difference set with a weighted product of $N=\binom n2$ regular $m$-gons, where $m=q^2+q+1$. The weights are chosen so that the resulting distances increase while the gaps between consecutive distances decrease. After normalizing the smallest gap to $1$, all distinct pairwise distances are separated by at least $1$, while the diameter has asymptotic constant $1-1/π^2<1$.

title: Strongly log-concave measures and lattices
abstract: Let $Λ\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full rank lattice with the property that $\det Γ\ge 1$ for all sublattices $Γ\subseteq Λ^*$. Moreover, the existence of such a density characterizes this property up to a universal dilation. There are a few consequences of the above. We list some. First, for such lattices we can bound the covering radius \[ μ(Λ, K) = \max_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\min_{λ\inΛ} \left\|x-λ\right\|_K \le \sqrt{\frac{2e}π} \cdot \mathbb{E}\,\left\|G\right\|_K \] of a convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $0$ in its interior, where $G \sim N(0,\mathrm{Id})$. title: Near-optimal Turán densities of $r$-graphs on $r+1$ vertices

title: RG-Invariant Symmetry Ratio for QCD: A Study of $U(1)_A$ and Chiral Symmetry Restoration

At each lattice spacing we observe a clear hierarchy $κ_{PS} > κ_{VA} > κ_{TX}$. title: Uniform ergodicity and spectral gap of importance-tempered MCMC with heavy-tailed targets
abstract: We study the importance-tempered random-walk Metropolis (RWM) algorithm on $\mathbb{R}^d$, which targets the tempered density $π_β(x) \propto π(x)^β$ with $β\in (0,1)$ and corrects for the resulting bias by importance weighting. The dynamics of this sampler can be described by a continuous-time Markov chain whose embedded chain is the tempered RWM. We prove that when the tails of $π$ decay at rate $\|x\|^{-γ}$, this continuous-time chain is uniformly ergodic if and only if $d/γ< β< (γ- 2)/γ$. title: A partial result towards the Chowla--Milnor conjecture
abstract: The Chowla--Milnor conjecture predicts the linear independence of certain Hurwitz zeta values. In this paper, we prove that for any fixed integer $k \geqslant 2$, the dimension of the $\mathbb{Q}$-linear span of $ζ(k,a/q)-(-1)^{k}ζ(k,1-a/q)$ ($1 \leqslant a < q/2$, $\gcd(a,q)=1$) is at least $(c -o(1)) \cdot \log q$ as the positive integer $q \to +\infty$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. It is well known that $ζ(k,a/q)+(-1)^{k}ζ(k,1-a/q) \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}π^k$, but much less is known previously for $ζ(k,a/q)-(-1)^{k}ζ(k,1-a/q)$. Our proof is similar to those of Ball--Rivoal (2001) and Zudilin (2002) concerning the linear independence of Riemann zeta values. However, we use a new type of rational functions to construct linear forms.

title: On The Rational Realization of Even-dimensional Spheres and Products of Eilenberg--MacLane Spaces as Classifying Spaces
abstract: In this paper, we study the rational realization problem for the classifying space $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)$.
